newsitem.title: CANADA: BHP Canada diamond mine poised for OK.
newsitem.headline: BHP Canada diamond mine poised for OK.

text.p: Canadian Northern Development Minister Ron Irwin said on Tuesday that final government approval of a diamond mine in Canada's Arctic proposed by Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd and Dia Met Minerals Ltd appeared likely to occur in early October.
"Everybody's working toward that deadline...it has the feel that it can be put together," Irwin told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
The Canadian government approved the project in principle in August and set a 60-day period for granting final approval.

The approval depends on reaching an environmental agreement between the two companies and Ottawa, which will ensure that all recommendations of an environmental review and environmental commitments are kept. BHP also has to negotiate impact benefits with Native communities in the Northwest Territories.

"Everybody is upbeat, they are positive, they like the idea of the 60-day period because they're all concentrating on closing things that would have been left over for years," Irwin said. "No one has signed yet, but they're all upbeat... It has a feel it could be closed."
The sixty-day period expires around October 7. The mine, which will be the first diamond project in Canada, is expected to cost C$860 million (US$628 million).
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
